newsitem.title: USA: PG&E shuts Calif. Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit.
newsitem.headline: PG&E shuts Calif. Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear unit.

text.p: PG&E Corp said Wednesday it had manually shut its 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power plant for repairs.
The San Francisco-based utility said it did not yet know how long the plant, at Avila Beach on California's central coast, would likely be shut.
"It's a problem in the feedwater system," said PG&E spokesman Jeff Lewis. "We're not sure how long the unit will be shut."

The unit was taken off line at about 0500 PDT/0800 EDT and is being kept on hot standby, which means the reactor is still active and typically indicates plant engineers expect the outage to be short term.
The facility's neighboring unit, Diablo Canyon 1, rated at 1,087 MW, was still operating at full power, he said.
Lewis said the company did not anticipate problems meeting electricity demand despite the outage at Diablo Canyon 2.
